# Meridian AI Corp - Deal Desk Concession Playbook (Enterprise Tier)

## 1 How to Use This Matrix

Every row below carries one of three dispositions. ACCEPT means the concession is pre-approved:
outside counsel or the deal desk may agree to it in writing without further internal approval.
COUNTER means we do not accept the customer's formulation but an approved fallback exists, and
the deal desk may sign off on that fallback. ESCALATE means neither outside counsel nor the deal
desk has authority to agree, in whole or in part, and the item must be routed under Section 8.
Anything not addressed in this matrix is COUNTER by default. Nothing in this matrix authorizes
agreement "in principle" or "subject to documentation" on an ESCALATE row.

## 2 Liability and Indemnity

Standard position: mutual aggregate cap at fees paid or payable in the trailing twelve months,
with the usual exclusions for payment obligations, fraud, and willful misconduct.

COUNTER any customer demand for uncapped, unlimited, or "unlimited as to amount" liability for
data, confidentiality, security, or privacy claims. The approved fallback is a supercap of three
times (3x) the trailing twelve-month fees, applied to breach of confidentiality obligations,
Security Incidents, and Provider's IP indemnity, with the general cap otherwise unchanged. Deal
desk may sign the 3x supercap without escalation.

ESCALATE any residual demand for uncapped or unlimited exposure in any category. Uncapped
liability has never been approved on any Meridian order: our insurance tower does not respond
above its limits, an uncapped indemnity is a going-concern exposure for a company of our size,
and it is a diligence disclosure item in any financing. Do not agree to a supercap above 3x, and
do not accept "direct damages are uncapped" or "the cap does not apply to Section X" drafting
that reaches the same result by another route.

## 3 Intellectual Property, Feedback, and Integrations

ACCEPT: a customer's request to retain ownership of its own Feedback. We do not need to own
Feedback; we need to be able to use it.

COUNTER any demand that Meridian assign Feedback, integration work product, connectors,
adapters, data mappings, or configurations. The approved fallback has two halves: (a) the
customer keeps ownership of its Feedback and grants Meridian a perpetual, irrevocable,
worldwide, royalty-free, sublicensable license to use it; and (b) integration work product and
all derivative works of the Platform remain Meridian property, with the customer receiving a
nonexclusive license to use them with the Platform during the term. Professional-services fees
buy the customer a deployment, not the engineering that produced it.

ESCALATE any assignment, escrow, or exclusive license of Meridian source code, model weights, or
core platform components, however the customer characterizes it. Assignment language framed as
"work made for hire" reaches core platform components whenever our connectors reuse shared
libraries, which is the ordinary case.

## 4 Customer Data and Model Training

ACCEPT (pre-approved): a carve-out prohibiting use of Customer Data, prompts, inputs, and
Outputs to train, fine-tune, or improve generalized or cross-customer models, including deletion
on termination. This concession is pre-approved for any order above USD 500,000 in annual
contract value and does not require escalation. Product has confirmed we do not train on
customer content on the enterprise tier.

Condition on that acceptance: we must preserve the Section 4.3 right to generate and use
aggregated, de-identified service analytics, including usage, performance, and reliability
telemetry, for operating, securing, and improving the Platform. Do not accept training carve-out
language that also sweeps in "usage data," "telemetry," or "service analytics," which would
disable our reliability and abuse-detection tooling across the customer base.

## 5 Audit and Security Assurance

Standard assurance package: annual SOC 2 Type II report, penetration-test summary, and a
completed security questionnaire once per contract year.

COUNTER any unlimited, on-demand, continuous, or "at any time" on-site audit or inspection right.
The approved fallback is: one on-site audit per contract year, plus one following any Security
Incident affecting the customer's data, on thirty (30) days' prior written notice, during normal
business hours, at the customer's expense, subject to confidentiality and site-access
requirements, conducted by an independent auditor who is not a Meridian competitor, and scoped to
the systems and facilities used to provide the Services.

ESCALATE any demand for audit of the model development or training environment, for access to
other customers' environments, or for regulator-style examination rights.

## 6 Exclusivity, Non-Compete, and Channel Restrictions

ESCALATE - no exception, no exercise of judgment. Neither outside counsel nor the deal desk has
authority to agree to any exclusivity, vertical non-compete, named-competitor restriction, or
other limit on whom Meridian may sell to, whether or not it is time-limited, revenue-limited, or
framed as a right of first refusal. These provisions constrain the company's addressable market,
are a mandatory disclosure item in financing and acquisition diligence, and have been the
subject of a standing board instruction since the Series A. Written CEO sign-off is required
before any position is communicated, and no counter-language may be circulated to the customer
before that decision is recorded.

## 7 Commercial Terms

Deal desk holds discount authority to 20% off list on annual commitments above USD 500,000, and
to 25% where the customer accepts a three-year term with annual uplift of at least 4%. Payment
terms of net 60 are pre-approved; net 90 requires CFO approval. Logo and reference rights should
be requested in every enterprise negotiation and traded away last.

## 8 Escalation Protocol

To escalate: state the item, the customer's exact language, the business impact, and the
recommended position in writing to the deal desk within one business day; do not send the
customer counter-language, a fallback, or a signal of where we might land. CEO sign-off must be
in writing and is recorded in the deal desk log before any response goes out. Escalation is not
a delay tactic and it is not optional; an item routed to ESCALATE that is conceded without
sign-off is treated as an authority breach regardless of the commercial outcome.

# Calloway Retail Group, Inc. - Markup Memorandum to Meridian Standard Terms

To: Meridian AI Corp, Legal and Deal Desk

From: Calloway Retail Group, Inc., Enterprise Technology Sourcing and Legal

Re: Meridian Standard Terms for Enterprise Platform Services v4.2 - required changes

Order value: USD 900,000 per year, three-year initial term

## 1.1 Scope and Process

This memorandum states the changes Calloway requires to Meridian Standard Terms v4.2 before
Calloway will execute the Order Form. Each request identifies the Meridian section at issue and
sets out Calloway's proposed replacement language. Calloway's Enterprise Risk Committee has
designated Requests 1 and 5 as conditions of approval; the remaining requests are delegated to
sourcing. Please respond position by position rather than returning a full redline, and note
that Calloway does not treat "these are our standard terms" as a response to any request.

## 2.1 Request 1 - Uncapped Liability for Data, Security, and Privacy Claims

Meridian Section 11.1 caps each party's total liability at the fees paid in the preceding twelve
months. For this order that ceiling is approximately USD 900,000, which is not a credible remedy
for an incident affecting Calloway loyalty records, payment metadata, or the personal data of
approximately 190,000 associates. Calloway's information-security addendum has required uncapped
exposure for these categories on every enterprise engagement since 2023, and sourcing has no
delegated authority to waive it.

Proposed language: "Notwithstanding Section 11.1, Provider's liability arising out of or
relating to breach of its confidentiality obligations, any Security Incident, or any violation
of applicable data protection law shall not be subject to any limitation of liability, whether
as to type or amount."

## 2.2 Request 2 - Ownership of Feedback and Integration Work Product

Meridian Section 6.1 assigns Provider ownership of both Feedback and integration work product.
Calloway funds the integration effort through professional-services fees and treats deliverables
it pays for as work made for hire. Calloway also cannot permit a supplier to commercialize
process knowledge derived from Calloway merchandising and replenishment workflows.

Proposed language: "Provider hereby irrevocably assigns to Customer all right, title, and
interest in and to (a) all Feedback provided by Customer or its personnel and (b) all
integrations, connectors, adapters, data mappings, configurations, and other work product
developed in connection with the Services, together with all derivative works thereof and all
intellectual property rights therein."

## 2.3 Request 3 - Prohibition on Training with Calloway Data

Meridian Sections 4.1 and 4.3 together permit Provider to use material derived from Calloway's
operations to improve the Platform. Calloway will not permit its data, or anything derived from
its data, to be used to improve a product that Meridian sells to competing retailers.

Proposed language: "Provider shall not use Customer Data, prompts, inputs, Outputs, usage data,
telemetry, or service analytics to train, fine-tune, evaluate, or otherwise improve any model,
service, or product, and shall delete all such material within thirty (30) days after
termination."

## 2.4 Request 4 - On-Site Audit and Inspection Rights

A SOC 2 Type II report prepared for Meridian's own purposes is not sufficient assurance for a
supplier processing Calloway payment metadata. Calloway requires the inspection rights it holds
with its logistics, payment, and fulfilment suppliers.

Proposed language: "Customer and its designated representatives may, at any time and from time
to time upon reasonable notice, enter and inspect any facility, system, or environment used by
Provider to provide the Services, and may audit Provider's books, records, personnel, and model
development environments, in order to verify compliance with this Agreement."

## 2.5 Request 5 - Retail-Vertical Exclusivity

Calloway is funding a category-defining deployment and a substantial internal change program.
Calloway will not underwrite a capability that Meridian resells to Calloway's direct competitors
during the same period. Meridian Section 13.1 is unacceptable as drafted.

Proposed language: "During the Term and for twelve (12) months thereafter, Provider shall not
license, sell, host, or otherwise make the Platform available to any of the entities listed on
Schedule E (Named Competitors) or to any retailer with annual worldwide revenue exceeding five
billion dollars (USD 5,000,000,000)."

## 3.1 Items Accepted Without Change

Calloway accepts Meridian Sections 1.1, 4.1, 5.1, 11.2, 12.1, and 15.2 as drafted and requires
no change to the Order Form pricing schedule or the implementation plan. Calloway's Enterprise
Risk Committee sits on the twentieth of each month; a complete response received after the
fifteenth will be carried to the following cycle.

protocol.quotes: Optional 'quotes' entries must reproduce cited section text verbatim. A quotation that does not appear in the cited section is a critical failure.

read_document.description: Read a document from the matter file, either in full or one numbered section.

section.description: Optional section number such as '4.2'. Omit for full text.

search_matter.description: Case-insensitive substring search across every document section.

query.description: Search phrase, three or more characters.

ask_client.description: Ask the client one natural-language factual question. Every question consumes budget, so ask only questions that could change the negotiating position.

escalate.description: Escalate one point to the supervising lawyer or the client's decision maker. Every escalation consumes budget, so escalate only departures from a non-negotiable position or requests that exceed your authority.

topic.description: Short label for the point escalated.

reason.description: Why this exceeds your authority or departs from the playbook.

submit_issue.description: Submit one material issue. Cite the single operative provision the issue targets as the FIRST citation, in the form '<document_id> §<section>'. Optional quotes must reproduce cited section text verbatim.

issue_id.description: Your own short label for this issue; reuse it in propose_redline.

citations.description: Provision citations such as 'msa §4.2'. Operative provision first.

quotes.description: Optional verbatim quotations supporting the issue. Text must appear verbatim in the cited section; paraphrase belongs in analysis.

revise_issue.description: Replace a previously submitted issue with a revised version. The issue_id must identify an existing issue. Only the latest version is used for scoring.

issue_id.description: Label of the issue to revise.

propose_redline.description: Propose replacement language for one section. Target the operative provision of the issue; link it to your submitted issue by reusing your issue_id label.

issue_id.description: Label of your submitted issue.

revise_redline.description: Replace the latest redline for an existing issue and provision. Only the latest version for that issue/document/section target is used for scoring.

submit_final.description: Submit the final summary for the supervising lawyer and end the episode. Submit only after all issues and redlines are in.

action.title: On-site audit and inspection rights
action.analysis: Calloway demands unrestricted on-site audit and inspection rights, which is an ESCALATE disposition in the playbook. The playbook permits one on-site audit per contract year, plus one following any Security Incident affecting the customer's data, on thirty (30) days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, at the customer's expense, subject to confidentiality and site-access requirements, conducted by an independent auditor who is not a Meridian competitor.
action.recommendation: Escalate to the CEO for sign-off.

quotes.text: Proposed language: "Customer and its designated representatives may, at any time and from time to time upon reasonable notice, enter and inspect any facility, system, or environment used by Provider to provide the Services, and may audit Provider's books, records, personnel, and model development environments, in order to verify compliance with this Agreement."

matter.title: Provider-Side Response to Customer Markup of AI Platform Terms
matter.assignment: Respond to the customer's markup memorandum on behalf of the provider. Take a position on each requested change - accept, counter, or escalate - grounded in the deal desk concession playbook, propose counter-language only where the playbook authorizes a fallback, ask the business team only questions that could change the position, and close with a short memorandum to the general counsel identifying the items that require CEO sign-off.

action.title: Retail-vertical exclusivity
action.analysis: Calloway demands exclusivity in the retail vertical for the duration of the agreement plus a twelve-month tail. This is an ESCALATE disposition in the playbook as it constrains Meridian's addressable market and is a mandatory disclosure item in financing and acquisition diligence. The playbook mandates CEO sign-off before any position is communicated.
action.recommendation: Escalate to the CEO for sign-off.

quotes.text: Proposed language: "During the Term and for twelve (12) months thereafter, Provider shall not license, sell, host, or otherwise make the Platform available to any of the entities listed on Schedule E (Named Competitors) or to any retailer with annual worldwide revenue exceeding five billion dollars (USD 5,000,000,000)."

action.summary:
In response to Calloway's markup memorandum, the following issues have been identified and addressed according to the Meridian Deal Desk Concession Playbook:

1. Uncapped liability for data, security, and privacy claims: Escalated to the CEO for sign-off.
2. Assignment of Feedback and integration work product: Escalated to the CEO for sign-off.
3. Prohibition on using Calloway data for training: Proposed counter-language that accepts the prohibition on training but excludes telemetry and service analytics.
4. On-site audit and inspection rights: Escalated to the CEO for sign-off.
5. Retail-vertical exclusivity: Escalated to the CEO for sign-off.

These items require CEO sign-off as per the playbook guidelines.
